newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen facing mild profit-taking at open.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen facing mild profit-taking at open.

text.p: The Dow industrials are likely to face mild profit-taking early in the session on Monday after their sharp run-up on Friday but analysts are far from calling an end to the latest rally in blue chips.
"In the absence of any major economic news today, I would not be a bit surprised to see some profit-taking early in the session," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained more than 53 points on Friday and will open at an all-time high of 6471.76.

As has been the case throughout its recent run, the Dow drew much of its strength on Friday from a small handful of names, most notably International Business Machines Corp, which continues to sizzle.
"Until IBM weakens, it's hard to say when we'll get a pullback in the Dow," Cardillo said.
Analysts said that even if the Dow succumbed to selling pressure at the open, its recent resilience left the outcome of the overall session in question.
"The momentum is still there," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities.
"We're probably going to open a little lower but you can't say we'll close lower," he said.
Wachtel also said that with the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday shortening the trading week, "we probably will see more activity than we generally see on a Monday."

The only economic indicator scheduled for release today is October existing home sales, due at 1000 EST/1500 GMT. Economists forecast the figure will stay roughly flat versus September's 4.0 million level.
In Tokyo, stocks finished with moderate gains. The Nikkei-225 index rose 77 points to 21,294.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index surged 36 points to 4055 amid mounting hopes of a prudent government budget.
However, U.S. shares traded in London were flat, with profit-taking keeping a lid on prices.
U.S. Treasuries were slightly lower. The benchmark 30-year bond eased 4/32, sending the yield up to 6.45 percent.
The dollar was stronger in Japan, where it pushed above the 112 yen level, and in Europe, where it neared 1.514 marks.
The December S&P 500 index future edged lower by 0.2 of a point to 751.00.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column takes a look at Genetics Institute Inc, whose shares have seen a flurry of speculative activity. According to the column, investors are wondering whether American Home Products will exercise an option to buy the Genetics Institute shares it does not already own for $85 per share. The option expires at the end of the year.
